title: “I Picked Myself Up Through Prayer and Soups”: Factors Impeding and Enhancing Long COVID Recovery Among Latinos in South Texas
abstract: ABSTRACT Aims We aimed to understand what factors have impeded and enhanced Long COVID recovery among Latinos in South Texas. Methods Through community partners, 78 participants were part of seven focus groups. We analyzed the data following Braun and Clarke's Reflexive Thematic Analysis. Results Factors that impeded recovery were: (1) Working while ill due to labor needs, expectations, and limited safety nets, (2) Mistrusting health care due to invalidating systemic barriers, (3) Grieving former self, and (4) Obsessing over the known and unknown. Factors that enhanced recovery were: (1) Focusing on a conscious fight to preserve life, (2) Leveraging cultural knowledge to reconnect with their sense of wholeness as a person, (3) Choosing Western medicine as one method of healing, and (4) Relying on God and trusted ones. Conclusion Long COVID recovery interventions among South Texas Latinos must account for structural and social determinants of health and cultural ways of healing.
